evidence.requirements: Nearly every requirement is met. The start page has the heading, Search and Family controls, the '<n> cartridges' count, and links whose text is exactly the record name (views.js:14-45; list.jpg). The detail view has all the facts, the water capacity with its source link, tables grouped by section with Symbol/Value/Unit columns, tolerances folded into the value (format.js:48-63), a Print button, an 'All cartridges' link and a bookmarkable hash route (app.js:40-58). The drawing has a title block and an accessible name '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:258). Print fits one A4 page with a footer (print.css; print-308_win.jpg). Two requirements are only partly met: (1) α has no angular dimension with arrowheads and extension lines; it is a single leader arrow onto the middle of the shoulder (drawing.js:160-177, item kind 'angle', one arrow). (2) Straight pistol and rimfire cases show 'Drawn as a straight case: α, L1, L2, H1, P2 not published' (geometry.js:224). Rule 4 defines these cases as straight, so the note reports values as missing that were never needed (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg).
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules and checks out against the references. The rim-type ratios (geometry.js:19-26) are correct. The chamfer is min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (geometry.js:161). The rimfire half-round has radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) (geometry.js:153-157). The groove, the belt ramp at δ up to R3/2 and the belt to E are right (geometry.js:175-186; detail-300_win_mag.jpg). The shoulder has fillets of r1 min and r2 (geometry.js:197-236). The bullet seating depth, k fraction, meplat, tangent ogive ρ and quarter ellipse match rule 7 (geometry.js:39-54, 253-276). The heeled 22 LR uses outside diameter H2 and heel diameter H2-2tb (geometry.js:247-260; detail-22_long_rifle.jpg shows the narrower heel inside the case). tn, tb, w and the primer pocket table follow rule 8 (geometry.js:29-36, 279-285); 9 mm Luger and 44 Mag show the 4.45/5.33 pockets, and the rimfire has none. Outlines and proportions match reference/308_win.png, 300_win_mag.png, 9_mm_luger.png and 22_long_rifle.png. Labels match the data ('α 10°58'0"', 'L3 51.18'), and the tables show values as published ('11.53 -0.2', '1°45'0"'). The 308 print fits one A4 page. Weak points: α is not drawn as an angle dimension. The straight-case inner wall uses an invented taper from tb to tn over one seating depth (geometry.js:290-296), visible as a kink in detail-44_rem_mag.jpg.
evidence.security: All data goes through escapeHtml (format.js:11-15) before it reaches innerHTML (views.js:19-22, 57-61, 96-111; drawing.js:243-259). A unit test checks escaping of markup in names (drawing-svg.test.js:97, views-list.test.js:33). There is no eval, Function or fetch; the data is a local script (index.html:19). An e2e network test asserts that no request goes beyond the app's own files (tests/e2e/network.test.js). The only external URL is a user-clicked source link with rel=noopener noreferrer.
evidence.code_quality: The modules are small and well separated (format, search, geometry, drawing, views, app), and each uses a UMD wrapper so both Node tests and file:// can load it. Functions map clearly to the rule numbers in comments (geometry.js:18,28,38). A drawing failure is contained so the tables still render (views.js:77-91). Readability suffers from dense one-line multi-statement code and short names (geometry.js:129-130, drawing.js:93-98). The layout() function is ~140 lines that mix label lanes, title-block search and the viewBox (drawing.js:83-220).
evidence.tests: Coverage is extensive and tied to the brief. The unit tests cover rim type for all 25 records, chamfer cap, rimfire half-round, belt, groove, fillets tangent to both lines, every bullet shape including the ogive centre, heeled bullet, walls, w, pocket table, and missing-value notes (geometry-*.test.js). Layout tests check no label overlaps, no label touching the outline, leaders not crossing labels, dimensions measuring the values at 1 unit = 1 mm, and printed text ≥ 2 mm (drawing-layout.test.js:57-148). The e2e tests run under both file:// and a static server and cover search, reload of the detail view, every value shown once, getBBox overlap, a 360 px screen, theme, one A4 print page for all 25, and network requests (tests/e2e/*.test.js).
evidence.ux_design: The drawings are legible with no overlapping labels (detail-*.jpg). The title block is clear, the tables are dense with tabular numbers and right-aligned values, and the facts sit in a compact grid. Dark mode is clean (test-output/shots/223_rem_dark_390_screen.png). Print is dense and well organised (print-308_win.jpg). Weaknesses: the dimension labels are large and bold relative to the part. The diameter dimensions run as vertical lines through the outline and the hatched section, and R1, E1 and P1 crowd into the 4 mm at the head. The drawing card leaves a large empty area to the left of the title block (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg).
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img with a <title> '<name> drawing' and a <desc> (drawing.js:256-259). The search and family controls have <label for> (views.js:36-39). The count is role=status with aria-live. The tables have <caption>, th scope=col and th scope=row (views.js:57-60). Focus moves to the heading on route change (app.js:53-56), and there is a :focus-visible outline (app.css:39). The muted text colour #566069 on #f6f6f3 has adequate contrast. Minor issues: very small uppercase header text (0.7rem, app.css:98), and no skip link.
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies and no build step; the only dev dependency is playwright (package.json). The app is about 1000 lines of JS for geometry, layout and views, which fits the problem. The label-lane and title-block placement algorithm is justified by the no-overlap rule. The generated data.js is a reasonable way to make file:// work.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives run, test and e2e instructions and explains why data.js is generated (README.md:15-25). Specs, the plan, research decisions (research.md 'Drawing: interpretation of the rules'), a task log and a test log are in specs/. The regression suite is broad, and package-lock.json is present. Gaps: there is no CI pipeline, no engines field or .nvmrc pinning Node 22, playwright uses a caret range, there is no changelog or release approach beyond version 1.0.0, and data.js must be rebuilt by hand after changing the JSONL.
evidence.visual_design: The look is calm and consistent: system sans for text, monospace for symbols and drawing labels, muted uppercase section captions, a restrained blue for dimensions, and a consistent card style across pages (list.jpg, detail-*.jpg). The bold monospace labels are heavy compared with the thin outline. The diameter leader lines and the large title block make the drawing look more like a diagram than a finished technical drawing.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: back link and Print, then the name, facts, the drawing, then the cartridge and chamber tables in a four-column grid (detail-308_win.jpg). The list is a full-width table. There is no clipping or overlap. The drawing area wastes vertical space: the labels stack below, and the title block leaves empty space on the left (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). The print layout packs the facts, drawing, five-column tables and footer onto one page (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.usability: Live search with alternative names (search.js) works, the family filter combines with the text search, the count updates, name links open the detail view, and the hash URL can be bookmarked and survives reload. There is a not-found view with a link back (views.js:47-51), and an empty-result message (views.js:15-16). Print is one click. Search filters are reset when returning to the list (app.js:21), a small friction point.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust it. The values are shown exactly as published, the drawings are computed to scale with section and pocket, the print is a clean one-page A4 sheet, and the source is cited. Professionals may object to the α leader instead of an angle dimension, the diameter lines drawn through the part, and the 'not published' notes on straight cases. These are polish issues, not trust breakers.

unmet_requirements: Shoulder angle α is labelled by a single leader arrow, not dimensioned with arrowheads and extension lines (drawing.js:160-177)
Straight pistol and rimfire cases carry a note claiming α, L1, L2, H1, P2 are 'not published' as missing values, although rule 4 defines them as straight cases (geometry.js:224)
strengths: The drawing geometry follows the brief's rules closely for every family (chamfer, groove, belt, rimfire half-round, shoulder fillets, tangent ogive, heeled bullet, walls, primer pocket) and matches the reference proportions

A rigorous test suite: unit tests for each rule plus layout overlap and scale checks, and e2e tests under file:// and http for reload, 360 px screens, theme, one A4 print page for all 25 records, and network isolation
Faithful data presentation (values as published, tolerances inline, d°m's" angles, mapped symbols), consistent HTML escaping, and a clean one-page A4 print with footer
issues: The shoulder angle α is not drawn as an angular dimension (no arc, no extension lines); only a leader arrow points at the shoulder

The drawing presentation is less professional than it should be: diameter dimension lines run through the outline and section, R1/E1/P1 crowd together at the head, labels are oversized, and much of the drawing card is empty space
Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no pinned Node version or exact devDependency, and a misleading 'not published' note on every straight case
review.verdict: This is a careful, well-tested build: geometry computed from the record's values that matches the references, values shown exactly as published, and a print view that fits one A4 page. It is close to publishable but needs a proper angular dimension for α, a cleaner placement of the diameter dimensions, and a CI pipeline first.
